recent_posts.title: A Recursive Algorithm to Render Signed Distance Fields
recent_posts.summary: Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) define 3D objects via mathematical functions and can be combined in powerful ways, but rendering them via raymarching is computationally expensive. A novel recursive divide-and-conquer algorithm is proposed and implemented in Rust that subdivides the view frustum into smaller quads, advancing all rays in a patch simultaneously and recursively splitting only when near a surface. This approach achieves 3–4x fewer rays per pixel and triples frame rate on a simple scene. An extension using linear interpolation for flat patches reduces samples to below one per pixel, reaching 100 FPS on a single M1 CPU core. The technique relates to the known but obscure GPU concept of 'cone marching' using multi-pass shaders. The results suggest CPU-based SDF rendering for real-time 3D games may be within reach with further optimization and multi-core usage.

recent_posts.title: Building a Copying GC for the Plush Programming Language
recent_posts.summary: A detailed account of implementing a copying garbage collector for Plush, a dynamically-typed language with actor-based parallelism. The implementation uses a dual-allocator design where each actor has a primary allocator for private allocations and a mailbox allocator for receiving messages, enabling lock-free allocation while supporting message passing between actors. The GC was completed in two weeks with help from a contributor, allowing long-running programs and real-time 3D graphics at 60 FPS, though some optimization work remains for handling large collections.

recent_posts.title: Optimizing the Plush Interpreter for Faster Raytracing
recent_posts.summary: A deep dive into optimizing the Plush interpreter through inline caching and code patching techniques. The author implements four key optimizations targeting hash lookup overhead in field access, method calls, and object construction, achieving a 3.5x performance improvement for a raytracer benchmark. The optimizations include inline caches for get_field and set_field instructions, constructor resolution improvements, and method call optimization, ultimately reducing single-threaded render time from 700ms to 196ms.

recent_posts.title: Out-Fibbing CPython with the Plush Interpreter
recent_posts.summary: A developer optimizes their custom Plush interpreter by implementing several bytecode-level improvements including instruction fusion, self-modifying code, and in-place stack operations. Starting with a recursive Fibonacci benchmark that ran slower than CPython (9.10s vs 5.70s), they achieved significant speedups through optimizations like combining push/call instructions, implementing lazy compilation with instruction patching, and creating specialized arithmetic instructions. The final result outperformed CPython at 4.57s, nearly doubling the original performance, though these microbenchmark improvements didn't translate to real-world raytracer performance gains.

recent_posts.title: Creating a Toy Programming Language with Actor-Based Parallelism
recent_posts.summary: A developer creates Plush, an experimental dynamically-typed programming language featuring actor-based parallelism for safe concurrent programming. The language uses isolated actors that communicate through message passing, avoiding traditional threading pitfalls. Performance tests show impressive results, with a raytracer achieving 15.9x speedup on a 16-core system. The project demonstrates how modern LLMs can assist in code generation for novel languages, despite critics claiming syntax similarity diminishes innovation. Key features include class-based inheritance for efficient object sharing between actors, flexible messaging systems, and independent memory allocation per actor.

recent_posts.title: AI Safety in the Presence of Multiple ASI Systems
recent_posts.summary: Explores the challenges of maintaining AI safety when multiple artificial superintelligence systems exist simultaneously. Discusses how competitive pressures between AI labs and nations could lead to cutting corners on safety measures, creating scenarios where unsafe AI systems might emerge alongside safe ones. Highlights the ongoing nature of AI safety as a problem that requires continuous attention rather than a one-time solution, particularly in a world with multiple competing entities developing AGI systems.

recent_posts.title: The case for humanoid robots in everyday life
recent_posts.summary: Several companies, including Boston Dynamics and Tesla, are working on creating useful humanoid robots to assist with household chores and provide aid to the elderly. The argument for humanoid robots is that our environment is designed for human-sized forms, making them more practical than wheeled or multi-legged robots. Additionally, imitation learning is easier with humanoid robots due to the abundance of data on human movements. Human-like robots could also minimize societal shock as they become more common.

recent_posts.title: My Low-Tech Attempt to Automate Spellchecking
recent_posts.summary: The author shares their experience of trying to automate spellchecking for their blog, highlighting limitations with available tools like aspell that produce many false positives. They explored using a neural network for better automation but faced hardware limitations. Eventually, they devised a simple, low-tech method by compiling lists of common misspellings and repetitive word patterns, which they found effective in reducing errors without generating false positives.

recent_posts.title: So I Rolled My Own Static Site Generator
recent_posts.summary: The author describes their journey of moving away from WordPress to creating their own static site generator using Rust. Motivated by frustrations with WordPress, they wrote their own markdown parser and CSS as a learning experience and for greater control over their blog. The new setup, hosted on GitHub Pages, supports old links and is designed for easy maintenance and minimal distraction. Future improvements may include automated checks and a portfolio page.

recent_posts.title: The Alternative Implementation Problem
recent_posts.summary: Avoid positioning your project as an alternative implementation as it puts you at the mercy of the canonical implementation. Joining forces with the canonical implementation and creating your own unique system are better strategies.
